complete_flat_problem.title: Kirby Problem 2.17
complete_flat_problem.statement:
Suppose that $c$ is a geodesic current on a hyperbolic surface,
and suppose that, on the space of hyperbolic metrics on the surface, $c$ has the same
length function as a closed geodesic.
Must $c$ be a convex combination of closed
curves?
complete_flat_problem.background:
Source: Kirby's Problems in Low-Dimensional Topology notes. Original problem number: KP-2.17.

Literature notes:
(1) For an introduction to the theory of geodesic currents in general, see the
foundational work of Bonahon [Bon86, Bon88], as well as the contem-
porary book of Erlandsson–Souto [ES22].
(2) As an example, suppose that $c_{1}$ and $c_{2}$ are so-called “length-twins,” i.e.,
non-homotopic closed curves that have the same length in any hyperbolic
metric. Then the geodesic current $\frac{1}{2}c_{1}+\frac{1}{2}c_{2}$ is not a closed curve, but it
will also have the same length as $c_{1}$ and $c_{2}$. It is a convex combination of
$c_{1}$ and $c_{2}$; thus, the question asks whether there exists some more exotic
type of current (for example one whose support in $\mathbb{H}^{2}$ is not a discrete set
of geodesics) that can also have the same length as either $c_{1}$ or $c_{2}$.

References cited:
- [Bon86] Francis Bonahon. Bouts des variétés hyperboliques de dimension 3. Annals of Mathematics, 124(1):71–158, 1986. URL: http://www.jstor.org/stable/1971388.
- [Bon88] Francis Bonahon. The geometry of Teichmüller space via geodesic currents. Inventiones mathematicae, 92(1):139–162, 1988. doi:10.1007/BF01393996.
- [ES22] Viveka Erlandsson and Juan Souto. Mirzakhani’s curve counting and geodesic currents, volume 345 of Progress in Mathematics. Birkhäuser/Springer, Cham, [2022] ©2022. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-08705-9.

<!-- LITERATURE-TRIAGE:BEGIN -->
## Literature review (checked 2026-08-17)

**Status:** open  
**Classification:** OPEN-TRIAGE

**Current literature assessment.** Length-twin convex combinations demonstrate the permitted phenomenon, but no classification excluding or constructing exotic geodesic currents was verified.

**Verified partial progress.**

- Convex combinations of length-twin closed curves have the same metric length function.

**Full solution or refutation.**

The existence of more exotic currents is open.

**What remains.**

Classify all currents with a closed-geodesic length function.

**Sources checked.**

- K3: A New Problem List in Low-Dimensional Topology, Problem 2.17 (2026). (authoritative_secondary): https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/kirbylistrep.pdf
  Evidence used: Explains length twins and poses the exotic-current question.

**Review notes.** No source alteration.

This is a dated literature triage; an open classification is not proof that no later or unindexed result exists.
